requirement.raw: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.
requirement.title: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics
requirement.summary: Build a new URL shortener service: Create a short link for a long URL; Durable storage of links and analytics; Click analytics per link; Horizontal scalability of the redirect path; Versioned REST API with a published contract. Also assumed: 5 capabilities required for production use.
capabilities: Create a short link for a long URL (stated)
Durable storage of links and analytics (stated)
Horizontal scalability of the redirect path (stated)
Versioned REST API with a published contract (stated)
Resolve a short code and redirect (HTTP 302) (assumed)
Reject unsafe or malformed target URLs (assumed)
Rate limiting and API-key protection of write endpoints (assumed)

nfrs.Scale targets: Design target 10k redirects/s peak, 100 creates/s, ~1B links over 5 years (read:write ~ 100:1). The prototype is sized for one node; the design scales out.
nfrs.Latency objective: p99 redirect latency < 50 ms inside the service (cache hit < 5 ms).
nfrs.Availability objective: 99.95% for redirects; creation and analytics may degrade first (analytics is best-effort and must never block redirects).
nfrs.Write access control: Write endpoints require an API key (X-API-Key); redirects and stats are public.
nfrs.Analytics privacy: Never store raw IPs: keep a salted, daily-rotating hash for unique-visitor counts.
nfrs.Analytics retention: Raw click events 90 days; daily aggregates kept for the life of the link.
nfrs.Analytics dimensions: Total and daily clicks, unique visitors, top referrer hosts, user-agent class. Geo-IP is out of scope for v1 (needs a licensed database).
nfrs.Abuse limits: 60 link creations per minute per API key (or per IP when keys are disabled).
nfrs.Short-code format: 7-character random base62 codes (62^7 = 3.5e12), unguessable, no sequential IDs.
nfrs.Default expiry: Links never expire unless the caller sets ttl_seconds.
nfrs.Custom aliases: Yes - custom aliases allowed, first-come-first-served, never overwritten.

acceptance_criteria.text: POST /api/v1/links with a valid http(s) URL returns 201 with a unique short code and short_url
GET /{code} returns 302 with Location set to the original URL; unknown codes return 404
Non-http(s), credential-bearing, local or private-network target URLs are rejected with 422
A custom alias can be requested; a taken alias returns 409 and never overwrites the existing link
Links may carry a TTL; expired links return 410 Gone
Links and analytics survive a process restart
Every redirect records a click; the stats endpoint returns totals, per-day counts, top referrers and user-agent classes
Raw client IPs and full referrer URLs are never stored; raw events are purgeable after the retention window
Code allocation is collision-safe under concurrent writers (no duplicate codes, no lost or overwritten links)
Redirects are served from cache after first access and analytics recording never blocks or fails a redirect
Link creation is rate limited per client (429 + Retry-After); write endpoints require an API key when configured; only owners can disable a link
The HTTP API conforms exactly to the published OpenAPI contract; errors use application/problem+json

ambiguities.question: 'scalable' is not measurable. What peak redirect throughput and total link volume must the service support?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Design target 10k redirects/s peak, 100 creates/s, ~1B links over 5 years (read:write ~ 100:1). The prototype is sized for one node; the design scales out.

ambiguities.question: What latency objective applies to redirects?
ambiguities.default_assumption: p99 redirect latency < 50 ms inside the service (cache hit < 5 ms).

ambiguities.question: What availability target applies, and may link creation degrade before redirects?
ambiguities.default_assumption: 99.95% for redirects; creation and analytics may degrade first (analytics is best-effort and must never block redirects).

ambiguities.question: Who may create and delete links? Is an API key required for write endpoints?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Write endpoints require an API key (X-API-Key); redirects and stats are public.

ambiguities.question: Which visitor data may analytics store? (raw IPs are personal data under GDPR)
ambiguities.default_assumption: Never store raw IPs: keep a salted, daily-rotating hash for unique-visitor counts.

ambiguities.question: How long must raw click events be retained?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Raw click events 90 days; daily aggregates kept for the life of the link.

ambiguities.question: Which analytics are required (clicks, uniques, referrers, devices, geography)?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Total and daily clicks, unique visitors, top referrer hosts, user-agent class. Geo-IP is out of scope for v1 (needs a licensed database).

ambiguities.question: What creation rate per client is acceptable before throttling?
ambiguities.default_assumption: 60 link creations per minute per API key (or per IP when keys are disabled).

ambiguities.question: How long may short codes be, and must they be unguessable?
ambiguities.default_assumption: 7-character random base62 codes (62^7 = 3.5e12), unguessable, no sequential IDs.

ambiguities.question: Should links expire by default? If so after how many days?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Links never expire unless the caller sets ttl_seconds.

ambiguities.question: Are caller-chosen custom aliases allowed?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Yes - custom aliases allowed, first-come-first-served, never overwritten.

out_of_scope: Malware/phishing reputation lookups (documented as production follow-up)

risks.title: Service used for phishing / malware redirection
risks.mitigation: URL safety validation, API keys, per-key rate limits, owner disable; add Safe Browsing lookup + WAF bot rules in production

risks.title: Enumeration of short codes exposing private links
risks.mitigation: Random 7+ char codes (3.5e12 space), negative caching, WAF rate rules on 404 bursts

risks.title: Viral link creates a hot partition / cache stampede
risks.mitigation: Read-through cache in front of the store; DynamoDB adaptive capacity; request coalescing (future) for cold misses

risks.title: Click events lost under overload or crash (in-memory buffer)
risks.mitigation: Bounded queue with drop counters on /healthz; flush on SIGTERM; durable stream (Kinesis) in prod

risks.title: Analytics retaining personal data beyond purpose
risks.mitigation: No raw IPs, referrer reduced to host, retention purge for raw events

risks.title: Prototype uses SQLite and in-process cache/limiter (single node)
risks.mitigation: All are behind ports; production adapters listed in the architecture; limiter must move to a shared store before scaling out

risks.title: Assumption not confirmed by a human: scalable
risks.mitigation: Defaulted to: Design target 10k redirects/s peak, 100 creates/s, ~1B links over 5 years (read:write ~ 100:1). The prototype is sized for one node; the design scales out.. Confirm before production; the value is configurable.

tradeoffs.chosen: Random base62 (CSPRNG) + uniqueness constraint + bounded retry
tradeoffs.alternatives: Global counter + base62; hash(url) truncation; pre-allocated key ranges (KGS)
tradeoffs.rationale: No coordinator or hot counter, codes are unguessable (no enumeration), collisions are detectable atomically by the store. Cost: one extra write attempt in ~1e-3 cases at 1B links.
301 is cached by browsers forever, so clicks after the first are invisible to analytics and disabling/expiring a link would not take effect. 302 costs one round-trip per click.

tradeoffs.chosen: Asynchronous bounded queue, batch writes, drop on overload
tradeoffs.alternatives: Synchronous write per redirect; exactly-once streaming
tradeoffs.rationale: Redirect latency/availability is the product; analytics is best-effort. Drops are counted and exposed on /healthz so loss is observable, not silent.

tradeoffs.chosen: Raw events (bounded retention) + pre-aggregated daily counters
tradeoffs.rationale: Totals stay O(days) to query and survive raw-event purging (privacy/retention); raw window still supports referrer/UA breakdowns.

tradeoffs.chosen: Key-value semantics behind a port (SQLite in prototype, DynamoDB in prod)
tradeoffs.rationale: Access pattern is single-key get/put at very high read volume; KV gives predictable latency and horizontal scale without sharding logic.
Unique-visitor counts without retaining personal data or enabling cross-day tracking.
Zero runtime dependencies for the prototype and fully in-process tests; the adapter is thin (one module) and can be swapped without touching service or storage code.

failure_scenarios: Cached links keep redirecting; uncached -> 5xx; creates fail fast. Prod: multi-AZ DynamoDB, alarms on throttles/errors.
Redirects unaffected (bounded queue); events dropped and counted on /healthz; flusher survives write errors.
Bounded retry (5) then 503 code_space_exhausted - signals code length is too short for volume instead of looping.
Storage uniqueness constraint arbitrates; exactly one writer wins, others get 409 - verified by a concurrent test.
Link disabled while cached on other nodes
Local cache is invalidated immediately; other nodes converge within cache TTL (60s). Prod: publish invalidations or lower TTL.
Per-key token bucket returns 429 with Retry-After; owner can disable links.
Up to one flush interval of click events lost (in-memory buffer); links are durable. Prod: durable stream (Kinesis) closes the gap.

Traceability: every acceptance criterion covered by at least one passing test
Pre-production: Load test (k6/Locust) at 2x target peak: redirect p99 < 50 ms, 0 errors, cache hit > 90%
Soak test 24h: memory flat, analytics backlog bounded
Chaos: stop analytics store (redirects unaffected), throttle link store (graceful 5xx)
Security: DAST on API, abuse simulation against rate limits
Production: Canary 5% with automated rollback on p99/5xx SLO burn
Synthetic probes: create -> redirect -> stats every minute per region
